\doxysubsection{Detailed Description}
\subsubsection*{template$<$typename T$>$\newline
struct cimg\+\_\+library\+\_\+suffixed\+::\+CImg$<$ T $>$}
Class representing an image (up to 4 dimensions wide), each pixel being of type {\ttfamily T}. 

This is the main class of the CImg Library. It declares and constructs an image, allows access to its pixel values, and is able to perform various image operations.

\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Image representation}

\end{DoxyParagraph}
A CImg image is defined as an instance of the container {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$}, which contains a regular grid of pixels, each pixel value being of type {\ttfamily T}. The image grid can have up to 4 dimensions\+: width, height, depth and number of channels. Usually, the three first dimensions are used to describe spatial coordinates {\ttfamily (x,y,z)}, while the number of channels is rather used as a vector-\/valued dimension (it may describe the R,G,B color channels for instance). If you need a fifth dimension, you can use image lists {\ttfamily CImg\+List$<$\+T$>$} rather than simple images {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$}.

Thus, the {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} class is able to represent volumetric images of vector-\/valued pixels, as well as images with less dimensions (1d scalar signal, 2d color images, ...). Most member functions of the class \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg}{CImg}\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}{\ttfamily T\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}} are designed to handle this maximum case of (3+1) dimensions.

Concerning the pixel value type {\ttfamily T\+:} fully supported template types are the basic C++ types\+: {\ttfamily unsigned char, char, short, unsigned int, int, unsigned long, long, float, double, ... }. Typically, fast image display can be done using {\ttfamily CImg$<$unsigned char$>$} images, while complex image processing algorithms may be rather coded using {\ttfamily CImg$<$float$>$} or {\ttfamily CImg$<$double$>$} images that have floating-\/point pixel values. The default value for the template T is {\ttfamily float}. Using your own template types may be possible. However, you will certainly have to define the complete set of arithmetic and logical operators for your class.

\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Image structure}

\end{DoxyParagraph}
The {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} structure contains {\itshape six} fields\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily \+\_\+width} defines the number of {\itshape columns} of the image (size along the X-\/axis).
\item {\ttfamily \+\_\+height} defines the number of {\itshape rows} of the image (size along the Y-\/axis).
\item {\ttfamily \+\_\+depth} defines the number of {\itshape slices} of the image (size along the Z-\/axis).
\item {\ttfamily \+\_\+spectrum} defines the number of {\itshape channels} of the image (size along the C-\/axis).
\item {\ttfamily \+\_\+data} defines a {\itshape pointer} to the {\itshape pixel} {\itshape data} (of type {\ttfamily T}).
\item {\ttfamily \+\_\+is\+\_\+shared} is a boolean that tells if the memory buffer {\ttfamily data} is shared with another image.
\end{DoxyItemize}

You can access these fields publicly although it is recommended to use the dedicated functions width(), height(), depth(), spectrum() and ptr() to do so. \doxylink{classImage}{Image} dimensions are not limited to a specific range (as long as you got enough available memory). A value of {\itshape 1} usually means that the corresponding dimension is {\itshape flat}. If one of the dimensions is {\itshape 0}, or if the data pointer is null, the image is considered as {\itshape empty}. Empty images should not contain any pixel data and thus, will not be processed by \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg}{CImg} member functions (a \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgInstanceException}{CImg\+Instance\+Exception} will be thrown instead). Pixel data are stored in memory, in a non interlaced mode (See cimg\+\_\+storage).

\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Image declaration and construction}

\end{DoxyParagraph}
Declaring an image can be done by using one of the several available constructors. Here is a list of the most used\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Construct images from arbitrary dimensions\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$char$>$ img;} declares an empty image.
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$unsigned char$>$ img(128,128);} declares a 128x128 greyscale image with {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily char} pixel values.
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$double$>$ img(3,3);} declares a 3x3 matrix with {\ttfamily double} coefficients.
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$unsigned char$>$ img(256,256,1,3);} declares a 256x256x1x3 (color) image (colors are stored as an image with three channels).
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$double$>$ img(128,128,128);} declares a 128x128x128 volumetric and greyscale image (with {\ttfamily double} pixel values).
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$$>$ img(128,128,128,3);} declares a 128x128x128 volumetric color image (with {\ttfamily float} pixels, which is the default value of the template parameter {\ttfamily T}).
\item {\bfseries{Note\+:}} images pixels are {\bfseries{not automatically initialized to 0}}. You may use the function {\ttfamily fill()} to do it, or use the specific constructor taking 5 parameters like this\+: {\ttfamily CImg$<$$>$ img(128,128,128,3,0);} declares a 128x128x128 volumetric color image with all pixel values to 0.
\end{DoxyItemize}
\item Construct images from filenames\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$unsigned char$>$ img("{}image.\+jpg"{});} reads a JPEG color image from the file "{}image.\+jpg"{}.
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$float$>$ img("{}analyze.\+hdr"{});} reads a volumetric image (ANALYZE7.\+5 format) from the file "{}analyze.\+hdr"{}.
\item {\bfseries{Note\+:}} You need to install \href{http://www.imagemagick.org}{\texttt{ Image\+Magick}} to be able to read common compressed image formats (JPG,PNG, ...) (See cimg\+\_\+files\+\_\+io).
\end{DoxyItemize}
\item Construct images from C-\/style arrays\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$int$>$ img(data\+\_\+buffer,256,256);} constructs a 256x256 greyscale image from a {\ttfamily int\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}} buffer {\ttfamily data\+\_\+buffer} (of size 256x256=65536).
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$unsigned char$>$ img(data\+\_\+buffer,256,256,1,3);} constructs a 256x256 color image from a {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily char\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}} buffer {\ttfamily data\+\_\+buffer} (where R,G,B channels follow each others).
\end{DoxyItemize}

The complete list of constructors can be found \href{\#constructors}{\texttt{ here}}.
\end{DoxyItemize}

\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Most useful functions}

\end{DoxyParagraph}
The {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} class contains a lot of functions that operates on images. Some of the most useful are\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item operator()()\+: Read or write pixel values.
\item display()\+: displays the image in a new window. 
\end{DoxyItemize}

Pixel value type. 

Refer to the type of the pixel values of an image instance. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$\+::value\+\_\+type} type of a {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} is defined to be a {\ttfamily T}.
\item {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$\+::value\+\_\+type} is actually not used in CImg methods. It has been mainly defined for compatibility with STL naming conventions. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Destroy image. 

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The pixel buffer data() is deallocated if necessary, e.\+g. for non-\/empty and non-\/shared image instances.
\item Destroying an empty or shared image does nothing actually. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item When destroying a non-\/shared image, make sure that you will {\itshape not} operate on a remaining shared image that shares its buffer with the destroyed instance, in order to avoid further invalid memory access (to a deallocated buffer). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}

Construct empty image. 

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item An empty image has no pixel data and all of its dimensions width(), height(), depth(), spectrum() are set to {\ttfamily 0}, as well as its pixel buffer pointer data().
\item An empty image may be re-\/assigned afterwards, e.\+g. with the family of assign(unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int) methods, or by operator=(const CImg$<$t$>$\&). In all cases, the type of pixels stays {\ttfamily T}.
\item An empty image is never shared. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ img1,\ img2;\ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ two\ empty\ images.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img1.assign(256,256,1,3);\ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Re-\/assign\ 'img1'\ to\ be\ a\ 256x256x1x3\ (color)\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img2\ =\ img1.get\_rand(0,255);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Re-\/assign\ 'img2'\ to\ be\ a\ random-\/valued\ version\ of\ 'img1'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img2.assign();\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Re-\/assign\ 'img2'\ to\ be\ an\ empty\ image\ again.}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg_a48f4ff6bf27dcd351b04f3150e06d74e} 
template$<$typename T$>$ \\
\mbox{\hyperlink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg}{cimg\+\_\+library\+\_\+suffixed\+::\+CImg}}$<$ T $>$\+::\+CImg (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const unsigned int}]{size\+\_\+x}{, }\item[{const unsigned int}]{size\+\_\+y}{ = {\ttfamily 1}, }\item[{const unsigned int}]{size\+\_\+z}{ = {\ttfamily 1}, }\item[{const unsigned int}]{size\+\_\+c}{ = {\ttfamily 1}}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [inline]}, {\ttfamily [explicit]}}



Construct image with specified size. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em size\+\_\+x} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} width(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+y} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} height(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+z} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} depth(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+c} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} spectrum() (number of channels). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item It is able to create only {\itshape non-\/shared} images, and allocates thus a pixel buffer data() for each constructed image instance.
\item Setting one dimension {\ttfamily size\+\_\+x},{\ttfamily size\+\_\+y},{\ttfamily size\+\_\+z} or {\ttfamily size\+\_\+c} to {\ttfamily 0} leads to the construction of an {\itshape empty} image.
\item A {\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgInstanceException}{CImg\+Instance\+Exception}} is thrown when the pixel buffer cannot be allocated (e.\+g. when requested size is too big for available memory). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The allocated pixel buffer is {\itshape not} filled with a default value, and is likely to contain garbage values. In order to initialize pixel values during construction (e.\+g. with {\ttfamily 0}), use constructor CImg(unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,\+T) instead.

Construct a new image instance of size {\ttfamily size\+\_\+x} x {\ttfamily size\+\_\+y} x {\ttfamily size\+\_\+z} x {\ttfamily size\+\_\+c}, with pixels of type {\ttfamily T}, and initializes pixel values from the specified string {\ttfamily values}. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em size\+\_\+x} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} width(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+y} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} height(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+z} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} depth(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+c} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} spectrum() (number of channels). \\
\hline
{\em values} & Value string describing the way pixel values are set. \\
\hline
{\em repeat\+\_\+values} & Tells if the value filling process is repeated over the image. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to CImg(unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int), but it also fills the pixel buffer with values described in the value string {\ttfamily values}.
\item Value string {\ttfamily values} may describe two different filling processes\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Either {\ttfamily values} is a sequences of values assigned to the image pixels, as in {\ttfamily "{}1,2,3,7,8,2"{}}. In this case, set {\ttfamily repeat\+\_\+values} to {\ttfamily true} to periodically fill the image with the value sequence.
\item Either, {\ttfamily values} is a formula, as in {\ttfamily "{}cos(x/10)\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}sin(y/20)"{}}. In this case, parameter {\ttfamily repeat\+\_\+values} is pointless.
\end{DoxyItemize}
\item For both cases, specifying {\ttfamily repeat\+\_\+values} is mandatory. It disambiguates the possible overloading of constructor CImg(unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,\+T) with {\ttfamily T} being a {\ttfamily const char\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}.
\item A {\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgArgumentException}{CImg\+Argument\+Exception}} is thrown when an invalid value string {\ttfamily values} is specified. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}

Construct image with specified size and initialize pixel values from a memory buffer. 

Construct a new image instance of size {\ttfamily size\+\_\+x} x {\ttfamily size\+\_\+y} x {\ttfamily size\+\_\+z} x {\ttfamily size\+\_\+c}, with pixels of type {\ttfamily T}, and initializes pixel values from the specified {\ttfamily t\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}} memory buffer. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em values} & Pointer to the input memory buffer. \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+x} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} width(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+y} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} height(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+z} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} depth(). \\
\hline
{\em size\+\_\+c} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} spectrum() (number of channels). \\
\hline
{\em is\+\_\+shared} & Tells if input memory buffer must be shared by the current instance. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item If {\ttfamily is\+\_\+shared} is {\ttfamily false}, the image instance allocates its own pixel buffer, and values from the specified input buffer are copied to the instance buffer. If buffer types {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t} are different, a regular static cast is performed during buffer copy.
\item Otherwise, the image instance does {\itshape not} allocate a new buffer, and uses the input memory buffer as its own pixel buffer. This case requires that types {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t} are the same. Later, destroying such a shared image will not deallocate the pixel buffer, this task being obviously charged to the initial buffer allocator.
\item A {\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgInstanceException}{CImg\+Instance\+Exception}} is thrown when the pixel buffer cannot be allocated (e.\+g. when requested size is too big for available memory). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item You must take care when operating on a shared image, since it may have an invalid pixel buffer pointer data() (e.\+g. already deallocated). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordtype}{unsigned}\ \textcolor{keywordtype}{char}\ tab[256*256]\ =\ \{\ 0\ \};}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<unsigned\ char>\ img1(tab,256,256,1,1,\textcolor{keyword}{false}),\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ new\ non-\/shared\ image\ from\ buffer\ 'tab'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ img2(tab,256,256,1,1,\textcolor{keyword}{true});\ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ new\ shared-\/image\ from\ buffer\ 'tab'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{tab[1024]\ =\ 255;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Here,\ 'img2'\ is\ indirectly\ modified,\ but\ not\ 'img1'.}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

Construct image copy. 

Construct a new image instance with pixels of type {\ttfamily T}, as a copy of an existing {\ttfamily CImg$<$t$>$} instance. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image to copy. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Constructed copy has the same size width() x height() x depth() x spectrum() and pixel values as the input image {\ttfamily img}.
\item If input image {\ttfamily img} is {\itshape shared} and if types {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t} are the same, the constructed copy is also {\itshape shared}, and shares its pixel buffer with {\ttfamily img}. Modifying a pixel value in the constructed copy will thus also modifies it in the input image {\ttfamily img}. This behavior is needful to allow functions to return shared images.
\item Otherwise, the constructed copy allocates its own pixel buffer, and copies pixel values from the input image {\ttfamily img} into its buffer. The copied pixel values may be eventually statically casted if types {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t} are different.
\item Constructing a copy from an image {\ttfamily img} when types {\ttfamily t} and {\ttfamily T} are the same is significantly faster than with different types.
\item A {\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgInstanceException}{CImg\+Instance\+Exception}} is thrown when the pixel buffer cannot be allocated (e.\+g. not enough available memory).

Advanced copy constructor. 

Construct a new image instance with pixels of type {\ttfamily T}, as a copy of an existing {\ttfamily CImg$<$t$>$} instance, while forcing the shared state of the constructed copy. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image to copy. \\
\hline
{\em is\+\_\+shared} & Tells about the shared state of the constructed copy. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to CImg(const CImg$<$t$>$\&), except that it allows to decide the shared state of the constructed image, which does not depend anymore on the shared state of the input image {\ttfamily img\+:} 
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item If {\ttfamily is\+\_\+shared} is {\ttfamily true}, the constructed copy will share its pixel buffer with the input image {\ttfamily img}. For that case, the pixel types {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t} {\itshape must} be the same.
\item If {\ttfamily is\+\_\+shared} is {\ttfamily false}, the constructed copy will allocate its own pixel buffer, whether the input image {\ttfamily img} is shared or not.
\end{DoxyItemize}
\item A {\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgArgumentException}{CImg\+Argument\+Exception}} is thrown when a shared copy is requested with different pixel types {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Construct image with dimensions borrowed from another image. 

Construct a new image instance with pixels of type {\ttfamily T}, and size get from some dimensions of an existing {\ttfamily CImg$<$t$>$} instance. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image from which dimensions are borrowed. \\
\hline
{\em dimensions} & C-\/string describing the image size along the X,Y,Z and C-\/dimensions. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to CImg(unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int), but it takes the image dimensions ({\itshape not} its pixel values) from an existing {\ttfamily CImg$<$t$>$} instance.
\item The allocated pixel buffer is {\itshape not} filled with a default value, and is likely to contain garbage values. In order to initialize pixel values (e.\+g. with {\ttfamily 0}), use constructor CImg(const CImg$<$t$>$\&,const char\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*},\+T) instead. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ CImg<float>\ img1(256,128,1,3),\ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ 'img1'\ is\ a\ 256x128x1x3\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ img2(img1,\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}xyzc"{}}),\ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ 'img2'\ is\ a\ 256x128x1x3\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ img3(img1,\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}y,x,z,c"{}}),\ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ 'img3'\ is\ a\ 128x256x1x3\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ img4(img1,\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}c,x,y,3"{}},0),\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ 'img4'\ is\ a\ 3x128x256x3\ image\ (with\ pixels\ initialized\ to\ '0').}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image from which dimensions are borrowed. \\
\hline

\hline

\end{DoxyItemize}

Construct image from a display window. 

Construct a new image instance with pixels of type {\ttfamily T}, as a snapshot of an existing {\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgDisplay}{CImg\+Display}} instance. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em disp} & Input display window. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The width() and height() of the constructed image instance are the same as the specified {\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgDisplay}{CImg\+Display}}.
\item The depth() and spectrum() of the constructed image instance are respectively set to {\ttfamily 1} and {\ttfamily 3} (i.\+e. a 2d color image).
\item The image pixels are read as 8-\/bits RGB values. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Access to a pixel value at a specified offset, using Neumann boundary conditions. 

Return a reference to the pixel value of the image instance located at a specified {\ttfamily offset}, or to the nearest pixel location in the image instance in case of out-\/of-\/bounds access. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em offset} & Offset to the desired pixel value. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to at(int,const T), except that an out-\/of-\/bounds access returns the value of the nearest pixel in the image instance, regarding the specified offset, i.\+e.
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item If {\ttfamily offset\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}0}, then {\ttfamily img}\mbox{[}0\mbox{]} is returned.
\item If {\ttfamily offset\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}=img.\+size()}, then {\ttfamily img}\mbox{[}img.\+size() -\/ 1\mbox{]} is returned.
\end{DoxyItemize}
\item Due to the additional boundary checking operation, this method is slower than operator()(). Use it when you are {\itshape not} sure about the validity of the specified pixel offset.
\item If you know your image instance is {\itshape not} empty, you may rather use the slightly faster method {\ttfamily \+\_\+at(int)}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Access to a pixel value at a specified offset, using Dirichlet boundary conditions. 

Return a reference to the pixel value of the image instance located at a specified {\ttfamily offset}, or to a specified default value in case of out-\/of-\/bounds access. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em offset} & Offset to the desired pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em out\+\_\+value} & Default value returned if {\ttfamily offset} is outside image bounds. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Writing {\ttfamily img.\+at(offset,out\+\_\+value)} is similar to {\ttfamily img\mbox{[}offset\mbox{]}}, except that if {\ttfamily offset} is outside bounds (e.\+g. {\ttfamily offset\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}0} or {\ttfamily offset\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}=img.\+size()}), a reference to a value {\ttfamily out\+\_\+value} is safely returned instead.
\item Due to the additional boundary checking operation, this method is slower than operator()(). Use it when you are {\itshape not} sure about the validity of the specified pixel offset. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Compute the arctangent of each pixel value. 

Replace each pixel value $I_{(x,y,z,c)}$ of the image instance by its arctangent $\mathrm{atan}(I_{(x,y,z,c)})$. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The \textbackslash{}inplace of this method statically casts the computed values to the pixel type {\ttfamily T}.
\item The \textbackslash{}newinstance returns a {\ttfamily CImg$<$float$>$} image, if the pixel type {\ttfamily T} is {\itshape not} float-\/valued. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Compute the arctangent2 of each pixel value. 

Replace each pixel value $I_{(x,y,z,c)}$ of the image instance by its arctangent2 $\mathrm{atan2}(I_{(x,y,z,c)})$. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}

\item The \textbackslash{}inplace of this method statically casts the computed values to the pixel type {\ttfamily T}.
\item The \textbackslash{}newinstance returns a {\ttfamily CImg$<$float$>$} image, if the pixel type {\ttfamily T} is {\itshape not} float-\/valued. 
\end{DoxyItemize}

Access to a pixel value, using Dirichlet boundary conditions for the X-\/coordinate. 

Return a reference to the pixel value of the image instance located at ({\ttfamily x},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}), or to a specified default value in case of out-\/of-\/bounds access along the X-\/axis. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em x} & X-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em y} & Y-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Z-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em c} & C-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em out\+\_\+value} & Default value returned if {\ttfamily }({\ttfamily x},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}) is outside image bounds. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to operator()(), except that an out-\/of-\/bounds access along the X-\/axis returns the specified value {\ttfamily out\+\_\+value}.
\item Due to the additional boundary checking operation, this method is slower than operator()(). Use it when you are {\itshape not} sure about the validity of the specified pixel coordinates. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item There is {\itshape no} boundary checking performed for the Y,Z and C-\/coordinates, so they must be inside image bounds. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}

Compute the cosine of each pixel value. 

Replace each pixel value $I_{(x,y,z,c)}$ of the image instance by its cosine $\cos(I_{(x,y,z,c)})$. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Pixel values are regarded as being in {\itshape radian}.
\item The \textbackslash{}inplace of this method statically casts the computed values to the pixel type {\ttfamily T}.
\item The \textbackslash{}newinstance returns a {\ttfamily CImg$<$float$>$} image, if the pixel type {\ttfamily T} is {\itshape not} float-\/valued. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Return pixel value, using cubic interpolation and Dirichlet boundary conditions for the X-\/coordinate. 

Return a cubicly-\/interpolated pixel value of the image instance located at ({\ttfamily fx},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}), or a specified default value in case of out-\/of-\/bounds access along the X-\/axis. The cubic interpolation uses Hermite splines. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em fx} & d X-\/coordinate of the pixel value (float-\/valued). \\
\hline
{\em y} & Y-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Z-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em c} & C-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em out\+\_\+value} & Default value returned if {\ttfamily }({\ttfamily fx},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}) is outside image bounds. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to linear\+\_\+at\+X(float,int,int,int,const T) const, except that the returned pixel value is approximated by a {\itshape cubic} interpolation along the X-\/axis.
\item The type of the returned pixel value is extended to {\ttfamily float}, if the pixel type {\ttfamily T} is not float-\/valued. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item There is {\itshape no} boundary checking performed for the Y,Z and C-\/coordinates, so they must be inside image bounds. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}

Return pixel value, using cubic interpolation and Neumann boundary conditions for the X-\/coordinate. 

Return a cubicly-\/interpolated pixel value of the image instance located at ({\ttfamily fx},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}), or the value of the nearest pixel location in the image instance in case of out-\/of-\/bounds access along the X-\/axis. The cubic interpolation uses Hermite splines. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em fx} & X-\/coordinate of the pixel value (float-\/valued). \\
\hline
{\em y} & Y-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Z-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em c} & C-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to cubic\+\_\+at\+X(float,int,int,int,const T) const, except that the returned pixel value is approximated by a cubic interpolation along the X-\/axis.
\item If you know your image instance is {\itshape not} empty, you may rather use the slightly faster method {\ttfamily \+\_\+cubic\+\_\+at\+X(float,int,int,int)}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item There is {\itshape no} boundary checking performed for the Y,Z and C-\/coordinates, so they must be inside image bounds. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}

Return a pointer to the first pixel value. 

Return a {\ttfamily T\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}, or a {\ttfamily const} {\ttfamily T\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}} pointer to the first value in the pixel buffer of the image instance, whether the instance is {\ttfamily const} or not. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The data() of an empty image is equal to {\ttfamily 0} (null pointer).
\item The allocated pixel buffer for the image instance starts from {\ttfamily data()} and goes to {\ttfamily data()+size() -\/ 1} (included).
\item To get the pointer to one particular location of the pixel buffer, use data(unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int,unsigned int) instead. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Return the number of image slices. 

Return the image depth, i.\+e. the image dimension along the Z-\/axis. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The depth() of an empty image is equal to {\ttfamily 0}.
\item depth() is typically equal to {\ttfamily 1} when considering usual 2d images. When depth(){\ttfamily \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}} {\ttfamily 1}, the image is said to be {\itshape volumetric}.
\item depth() returns an {\ttfamily int}, although the image depth is internally stored as an {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int}. Using an {\ttfamily int} is safer and prevents arithmetic traps possibly encountered when doing calculations involving {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variables. Access to the initial {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variable is possible (though not recommended) by {\ttfamily (\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}this).\+\_\+depth}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

{\em guide} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} used as the initial correspondence estimate for the algorithm. \textquotesingle{}guide\textquotesingle{} may have a last channel with boolean values (0=false \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} other=true) that tells for each pixel if its correspondence vector is constrained to its initial value (constraint mask). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Draw a 2d spline. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em x0} & X-\/coordinate of the starting curve point \\
\hline
{\em y0} & Y-\/coordinate of the starting curve point \\
\hline
{\em u0} & X-\/coordinate of the starting velocity \\
\hline
{\em v0} & Y-\/coordinate of the starting velocity \\
\hline
{\em x1} & X-\/coordinate of the ending curve point \\
\hline
{\em y1} & Y-\/coordinate of the ending curve point \\
\hline
{\em u1} & X-\/coordinate of the ending velocity \\
\hline
{\em v1} & Y-\/coordinate of the ending velocity \\
\hline
{\em color} & Pointer to {\ttfamily spectrum()} consecutive values of type {\ttfamily T}, defining the drawing color. \\
\hline
{\em precision} & Curve drawing precision. \\
\hline
{\em opacity} & Drawing opacity. \\
\hline
{\em pattern} & An integer whose bits describe the line pattern. \\
\hline
{\em init\+\_\+hatch} & If {\ttfamily true}, init hatch motif. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The curve is a 2d cubic Bezier spline, from the set of specified starting/ending points and corresponding velocity vectors.
\item The spline is drawn as a serie of connected segments. The {\ttfamily precision} parameter sets the average number of pixels in each drawn segment.
\item A cubic Bezier curve is sometimes defined by a set of 4 points \{ ({\ttfamily x0},{\ttfamily y0}), ({\ttfamily xa},{\ttfamily ya}), ({\ttfamily xb},{\ttfamily yb}), ({\ttfamily x1},{\ttfamily y1}) \} where ({\ttfamily x0},{\ttfamily y0}) is the starting point, ({\ttfamily x1},{\ttfamily y1}) is the ending point and ({\ttfamily xa},{\ttfamily ya}), ({\ttfamily xb},{\ttfamily yb}) are two {\itshape control} points. The starting and ending velocities ({\ttfamily u0},{\ttfamily v0}) and ({\ttfamily u1},{\ttfamily v1}) can be deduced easily from the control points as {\ttfamily u0} = ({\ttfamily xa} -\/ {\ttfamily x0}), {\ttfamily v0} = ({\ttfamily ya} -\/ {\ttfamily y0}), {\ttfamily u1} = ({\ttfamily x1} -\/ {\ttfamily xb}) and {\ttfamily v1} = ({\ttfamily y1} -\/ {\ttfamily yb}). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example\+:}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<unsigned\ char>\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(100,100,1,3,0);}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ \textcolor{keywordtype}{unsigned}\ \textcolor{keywordtype}{char}\ color[]\ =\ \{\ 255,255,255\ \};}
\DoxyCodeLine{\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}.draw\_spline(30,30,0,100,90,40,0,-\/100,color);}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

Return a CImg$<$\+T$>$\+::iterator pointing next to the last pixel value. 

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Writing {\ttfamily img.\+end()} is equivalent to {\ttfamily img.\+data() + img.\+size()}.
\item It has been mainly defined for compatibility with STL naming conventions. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The returned iterator actually points to a value located {\itshape outside} the acceptable bounds of the pixel buffer. Trying to read or write the content of the returned iterator will probably result in a crash. Use it mainly as a strict upper bound for a CImg$<$\+T$>$\+::iterator. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}

\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{for}\ (CImg<float>::iterator\ it\ =\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}.begin();\ it<\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}.end();\ ++it)\ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ 'img.end()'\ used\ here\ as\ an\ upper\ bound\ for\ the\ iterator.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ *it\ =\ 0;}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

Compute the exponential of each pixel value. 

Replace each pixel value $I_{(x,y,z,c)}$ of the image instance by its exponential $e^{I_{(x,y,z,c)}}$. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The \textbackslash{}inplace of this method statically casts the computed values to the pixel type {\ttfamily T}.
\item The \textbackslash{}newinstance returns a {\ttfamily CImg$<$float$>$} image, if the pixel type {\ttfamily T} is {\itshape not} float-\/valued. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

\item 1 = Forward finite differences

\end{DoxyItemize}\\

\item If {\ttfamily nb==0}, instance image is splitted into blocs of egal values along the specified axis.
\item If {\ttfamily nb\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}=0}, instance image is splitted into blocs of -\/{\ttfamily nb} pixel wide.
\item If {\ttfamily nb\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}0}, instance image is splitted into {\ttfamily nb} blocs. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Return the number of image rows. 

Return the image height, i.\+e. the image dimension along the Y-\/axis. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The height() of an empty image is equal to {\ttfamily 0}.
\item height() returns an {\ttfamily int}, although the image height is internally stored as an {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int}. Using an {\ttfamily int} is safer and prevents arithmetic traps possibly encountered when doing calculations involving {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variables. Access to the initial {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variable is possible (though not recommended) by {\ttfamily (\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}this).\+\_\+height}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Compute the histogram of pixel values. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em nb\+\_\+levels} & Number of desired histogram levels. \\
\hline
{\em min\+\_\+value} & Minimum pixel value considered for the histogram computation. All pixel values lower than {\ttfamily min\+\_\+value} will not be counted. \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+value} & Maximum pixel value considered for the histogram computation. All pixel values higher than {\ttfamily max\+\_\+value} will not be counted. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The histogram H of an image I is the 1d function where H(x) counts the number of occurences of the value x in the image I.
\item The resulting histogram is always defined in 1d. Histograms of multi-\/valued images are not multi-\/dimensional. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Test if pixel buffers of instance and input images overlap. 

Return {\ttfamily true}, if pixel buffers attached to image instance and input image {\ttfamily img} overlap, and {\ttfamily false} otherwise. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image to compare with. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Buffer overlapping may happen when manipulating {\itshape shared} images.
\item If two image buffers overlap, operating on one of the image will probably modify the other one.
\item Most of the time, {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} instances are {\itshape non-\/shared} and do not overlap between each others. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}

\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ img2\ =\ img1.get\_shared\_channel(1);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Get\ shared\ version\ of\ the\ green\ channel.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{if}\ (img1.is\_overlapped(img2))\ \{\ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Test\ succeeds,\ 'img1'\ and\ 'img2'\ overlaps.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ std::printf(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}Buffers\ overlap!\(\backslash\)n"{}});}
\DoxyCodeLine{\}}

Test shared state of the pixel buffer. 

Return {\ttfamily true} if image instance has a shared memory buffer, and {\ttfamily false} otherwise. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item A shared image do not own his pixel buffer data() and will not deallocate it on destruction.
\item Most of the time, a {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} image instance will {\itshape not} be shared.
\item A shared image can only be obtained by a limited set of constructors and methods (see list below). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Return pixel value, using linear interpolation and Dirichlet boundary conditions for the X-\/coordinate. 

Return a linearly-\/interpolated pixel value of the image instance located at ({\ttfamily fx},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}), or a specified default value in case of out-\/of-\/bounds access along the X-\/axis. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em fx} & X-\/coordinate of the pixel value (float-\/valued). \\
\hline
{\em y} & Y-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Z-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em c} & C-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em out\+\_\+value} & Default value returned if {\ttfamily }({\ttfamily fx},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}) is outside image bounds. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to at\+X(int,int,int,int,const T), except that the returned pixel value is approximated by a linear interpolation along the X-\/axis, if corresponding coordinates are not integers.
\item The type of the returned pixel value is extended to {\ttfamily float}, if the pixel type {\ttfamily T} is not float-\/valued. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item There is {\itshape no} boundary checking performed for the Y,Z and C-\/coordinates, so they must be inside image bounds. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}

Return pixel value, using linear interpolation and Neumann boundary conditions for the X-\/coordinate. 

Return a linearly-\/interpolated pixel value of the image instance located at ({\ttfamily fx},{\ttfamily y},{\ttfamily z},{\ttfamily c}), or the value of the nearest pixel location in the image instance in case of out-\/of-\/bounds access along the X-\/axis. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em fx} & X-\/coordinate of the pixel value (float-\/valued). \\
\hline
{\em y} & Y-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Z-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em c} & C-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to linear\+\_\+at\+X(float,int,int,int,const T) const, except that an out-\/of-\/bounds access returns the value of the nearest pixel in the image instance, regarding the specified X-\/coordinate.
\item If you know your image instance is {\itshape not} empty, you may rather use the slightly faster method {\ttfamily \+\_\+linear\+\_\+at\+X(float,int,int,int)}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item There is {\itshape no} boundary checking performed for the Y,Z and C-\/coordinates, so they must be inside image bounds. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}

Compute the logarithm of each pixel value. 

Replace each pixel value $I_{(x,y,z,c)}$ of the image instance by its logarithm $\mathrm{log}_{e}(I_{(x,y,z,c)})$. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The \textbackslash{}inplace of this method statically casts the computed values to the pixel type {\ttfamily T}.
\item The \textbackslash{}newinstance returns a {\ttfamily CImg$<$float$>$} image, if the pixel type {\ttfamily T} is {\itshape not} float-\/valued. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Transfer content of an image instance into another one. 

Transfer the dimensions and the pixel buffer content of an image instance into another one, and replace instance by an empty image. It avoids the copy of the pixel buffer when possible. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Destination image. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Pixel types {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t} of source and destination images can be different, though the process is designed to be instantaneous when {\ttfamily T} and {\ttfamily t} are the same. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ src(256,256,1,3,0),\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ a\ 256x256x1x3\ (color)\ image\ filled\ with\ value\ '0'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ dest(16,16);\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ a\ 16x16x1x1\ (scalar)\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{src.move\_to(dest);\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Now,\ 'src'\ is\ empty\ and\ 'dest'\ is\ the\ 256x256x1x3\ image.}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

Transfer content of an image instance into a new image in an image list. 

Transfer the dimensions and the pixel buffer content of an image instance into a newly inserted image at position {\ttfamily pos} in specified {\ttfamily CImg\+List$<$t$>$} instance. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em list} & Destination list. \\
\hline
{\em pos} & Position of the newly inserted image in the list. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item When optional parameter {\ttfamily pos} is ommited, the image instance is transfered as a new image at the end of the specified {\ttfamily list}.
\item It is convenient to sequentially insert new images into image lists, with no additional copies of memory buffer. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImgList<float>\ list;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ an\ empty\ image\ list.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}reference.jpg"{}});\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Read\ image\ from\ filename.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}.move\_to(list);\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Transfer\ image\ content\ as\ a\ new\ item\ in\ the\ list\ (no\ buffer\ copy).}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

In-\/place pointwise multiplication. 

Compute the pointwise multiplication between the image instance and the specified input image {\ttfamily img}. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image, as the second operand of the multiplication. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Similar to operator+=(const CImg$<$t$>$\&), except that it performs a pointwise multiplication instead of an addition.
\item It does {\itshape not} perform a {\itshape matrix} multiplication. For this purpose, use operator\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}=(const CImg$<$t$>$\&) instead. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}reference.jpg"{}}),}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ shade(\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}.width,\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}.height(),1,1,\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}-\/(x-\/w/2)\string^2-\/(y-\/h/2)\string^2"{}},\textcolor{keyword}{false});}
\DoxyCodeLine{shade.normalize(0,1);}

Implicitely cast an image into a {\ttfamily T\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}. 

Implicitely cast a {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} instance into a {\ttfamily T\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}} or {\ttfamily const} {\ttfamily T\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}} pointer, whether the image instance is {\itshape const} or not. The returned pointer points on the first value of the image pixel buffer. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item It simply returns the pointer data() to the pixel buffer.
\item This implicit conversion is convenient to test the empty state of images (data() being {\ttfamily 0} in this case), e.\+g. 
\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ img1(100,100),\ img2;\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ 'img1'\ is\ a\ 100x100\ image,\ 'img2'\ is\ an\ empty\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{if}\ (img1)\ \{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Test\ succeeds,\ 'img1'\ is\ not\ an\ empty\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \textcolor{keywordflow}{if}\ (!img2)\ \{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Test\ succeeds,\ 'img2'\ is\ an\ empty\ image.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ std::printf(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}'img1'\ is\ not\ empty,\ 'img2'\ is\ empty."{}});}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\}}

\end{DoxyCode}

\item It also allows to use brackets to access pixel values, without need for a {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$\+::operator\mbox{[}$\,$\mbox{]}()}, e.\+g. 
\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(100,100);}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ \textcolor{keywordtype}{float}\ value\ =\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}[99];\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Access\ to\ value\ of\ the\ last\ pixel\ on\ the\ first\ row.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}[510]\ =\ 255;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Set\ pixel\ value\ at\ (10,5).}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Access to a pixel value. 

Return a reference to a located pixel value of the image instance, being possibly {\itshape const}, whether the image instance is {\itshape const} or not. This is the standard method to get/set pixel values in {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$} images. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em x} & X-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em y} & Y-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em z} & Z-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
{\em c} & C-\/coordinate of the pixel value. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Range of pixel coordinates start from {\ttfamily (0,0,0,0)} to {\ttfamily (width() -\/ 1,height() -\/ 1,depth() -\/ 1,spectrum() -\/ 1)}.
\item Due to the particular arrangement of the pixel buffers defined in CImg, you can omit one coordinate if the corresponding dimension is equal to {\ttfamily 1}. For instance, pixels of a 2d image (depth() equal to {\ttfamily 1}) can be accessed by {\ttfamily img(x,y,c)} instead of {\ttfamily img(x,y,0,c)}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item There is {\itshape no} boundary checking done in this operator, to make it as fast as possible. You {\itshape must} take care of out-\/of-\/bounds access by yourself, if necessary. For debuging purposes, you may want to define macro {\ttfamily \textquotesingle{}cimg\+\_\+verbosity\textquotesingle{}\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}=3} to enable additional boundary checking operations in this operator. In that case, warning messages will be printed on the error output when accessing out-\/of-\/bounds pixels. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(100,100,1,3,0);\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ a\ 100x100x1x3\ (color)\ image\ with\ pixels\ set\ to\ '0'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ \textcolor{keywordtype}{float}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ valR\ =\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(10,10,0,0),\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Read\ red\ value\ at\ coordinates\ (10,10).}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ valG\ =\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(10,10,0,1),\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Read\ green\ value\ at\ coordinates\ (10,10)}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ valB\ =\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(10,10,2),\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Read\ blue\ value\ at\ coordinates\ (10,10)\ (Z-\/coordinate\ can\ be\ omitted).}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ avg\ =\ (valR\ +\ valG\ +\ valB)/3;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Compute\ average\ pixel\ value.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(10,10,0)\ =\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(10,10,1)\ =\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(10,10,2)\ =\ avg;\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Replace\ the\ color\ pixel\ (10,10)\ by\ the\ average\ grey\ value.}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

In-\/place multiplication operator. 

Replace the image instance by the matrix multiplication between the image instance and the specified matrix {\ttfamily img}. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Second operand of the matrix multiplication. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item It does {\itshape not} compute a pointwise multiplication between two images. For this purpose, use mul(const CImg$<$t$>$\&) instead.
\item The size of the image instance can be modified by this operator. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ A(2,2,1,1,\ 1,2,3,4);\ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ 2x2\ matrix\ A\ =\ [1,2;3,4].}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ CImg<float>\ X(1,2,1,1,\ 1,2);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ 1x2\ vector\ X\ =\ [1;2].}}
\DoxyCodeLine{A*=X;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Assign\ matrix\ multiplication\ A*X\ to\ 'A'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{comment}{//\ 'A'\ is\ now\ a\ 1x2\ vector\ whose\ values\ are\ [5;11].}}

\end{DoxyCode}
 
\end{DoxyParagraph}

Return a non-\/shared copy of the image instance. 

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Use this operator to ensure you get a non-\/shared copy of an image instance with same pixel type {\ttfamily T}. Indeed, the usual copy constructor CImg$<$\+T$>$(const CImg$<$\+T$>$\&) returns a shared copy of a shared input image, and it may be not desirable to work on a regular copy (e.\+g. for a resize operation) if you have no information about the shared state of the input image.
\item Writing {\ttfamily }(+img) is equivalent to {\ttfamily CImg$<$\+T$>$(img,false)}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

In-\/place increment operator (prefix). 

Add {\ttfamily 1} to all image pixels, and return a reference to the current incremented image instance. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Writing {\ttfamily ++img} is equivalent to {\ttfamily img+=1}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

In-\/place increment operator (postfix). 

Add {\ttfamily 1} to all image pixels, and return a new copy of the initial (pre-\/incremented) image instance. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Use the prefixed version operator++() if you don\textquotesingle{}t need a copy of the initial (pre-\/incremented) image instance, since a useless image copy may be expensive in terms of memory usage. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

In-\/place addition operator. 

Add values to image pixels, according to the values of the input image {\ttfamily img}. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image to add. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The size of the image instance is never modified.
\item It is not mandatory that input image {\ttfamily img} has the same size as the image instance. If less values are available in {\ttfamily img}, then the values are added periodically. For instance, adding one WxH scalar image (spectrum() equal to {\ttfamily 1}) to one WxH color image (spectrum() equal to {\ttfamily 3}) means each color channel will be incremented with the same values at the same locations. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ img1(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}reference.jpg"{}});\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Load\ a\ RGB\ color\ image\ (img1.spectrum()==3)}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ CImg<float>\ img2(img1.width(),\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}.height(),1,1,\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}255*(x/w)\string^2"{}});\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ a\ scalar\ shading\ (img2.spectrum()==1).}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img1+=img2;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Add\ shading\ to\ each\ channel\ of\ 'img1'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img1.cut(0,255);\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Prevent\ [0,255]\ overflow.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{(img2,img1).\mbox{\hyperlink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg_a901c891242e27a7e5bf7932767e80d60}{display}}();}

\end{DoxyCode}

In-\/place addition operator. 

Add specified {\ttfamily value} to all pixels of an image instance. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em value} & Value to add. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Resulting pixel values are casted to fit the pixel type {\ttfamily T}. For instance, adding {\ttfamily 0.\+2} to a {\ttfamily CImg$<$char$>$} is possible but does nothing indeed.
\item Overflow values are treated as with standard C++ numeric types. For instance, 
\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<unsigned\ char>\ \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}(100,100,1,1,255);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ a\ 100x100\ image\ with\ pixel\ values\ '255'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecimg__library__suffixed_a4b2be1eebcd69c87bde0b5757cad1938}{img}}+=1;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Add\ '1'\ to\ each\ pixels\ -\/>\ Overflow.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{comment}{//\ here\ all\ pixels\ of\ image\ 'img'\ are\ equal\ to\ '0'.}}

\end{DoxyCode}

\item To prevent value overflow, you may want to consider pixel type {\ttfamily T} as {\ttfamily float} or {\ttfamily double}, and use cut() after addition. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<unsigned\ char>\ img1(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}reference.jpg"{}});\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Load\ a\ 8-\/bits\ RGB\ image\ (values\ in\ [0,255]).}}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ img2(img1);\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Construct\ a\ float-\/valued\ copy\ of\ 'img1'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img2+=100;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Add\ '100'\ to\ pixel\ values\ -\/>\ goes\ out\ of\ [0,255]\ but\ no\ problems\ with\ floats.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img2.cut(0,255);\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Cut\ values\ in\ [0,255]\ to\ fit\ the\ 'unsigned\ char'\ constraint.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img1\ =\ img2;\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Rewrite\ safe\ result\ in\ 'unsigned\ char'\ version\ 'img1'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ CImg<unsigned\ char>\ img3\ =\ (img1\ +\ 100).\mbox{\hyperlink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg_a8dc8d6323707b649a8b1021b123757c8}{cut}}(0,255);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Do\ the\ same\ in\ a\ more\ simple\ and\ elegant\ way.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{(img1,img2,img3).\mbox{\hyperlink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg_a901c891242e27a7e5bf7932767e80d60}{display}}();}

Construct an image list from two images. 

Return a new list of image ({\ttfamily \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgList}{CImg\+List}} instance) containing exactly two elements\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item A copy of the image instance, at position \mbox{[}{\ttfamily 0}\mbox{]}.
\item A copy of the specified image {\ttfamily img}, at position \mbox{[}{\ttfamily 1}\mbox{]}.
\end{DoxyItemize}


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Input image that will be the second image of the resulting list. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The family of operator,() is convenient to easily create list of images, but it is also {\itshape quite} {\itshape slow} in practice (see warning below).
\item Constructed lists contain no shared images. If image instance or input image {\ttfamily img} are shared, they are inserted as new non-\/shared copies in the resulting list.
\item The pixel type of the returned list may be a superset of the initial pixel type {\ttfamily T}, if necessary. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyWarning}{Warning}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Pipelining operator,() {\ttfamily N} times will perform {\ttfamily N} copies of the entire content of a (growing) image list. This may become very expensive in terms of speed and used memory. You should avoid using this technique to build a new \doxylink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImgList}{CImg\+List} instance from several images, if you are seeking for performance. Fast insertions of images in an image list are possible with CImg\+List$<$\+T$>$\+::insert(const CImg$<$t$>$\&,unsigned int,bool) or move\+\_\+to(\+CImg\+List$<$t$>$\&,unsigned int). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyWarning}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ CImg<float>}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ img1(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}reference.jpg"{}}),}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ img2\ =\ img1.get\_mirror(\textcolor{charliteral}{'x'}),}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ img3\ =\ img2.get\_blur(5);}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{const}\ CImgList<float>\ list\ =\ (img1,img2);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Create\ list\ of\ two\ elements\ from\ 'img1'\ and\ 'img2'.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{(list,img3).\mbox{\hyperlink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg_a901c891242e27a7e5bf7932767e80d60}{display}}();\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Display\ image\ list\ containing\ copies\ of\ 'img1','img2'\ and\ 'img3'.}}

\end{DoxyCode}
  
\end{DoxyParagraph}

In-\/place division operator. 

Replace the image instance by the (right) matrix division between the image instance and the specified matrix {\ttfamily img}. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em img} & Second operand of the matrix division. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item It does {\itshape not} compute a pointwise division between two images. For this purpose, use div(const CImg$<$t$>$\&) instead.
\item It returns the matrix operation {\ttfamily A\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}inverse}(img).
\item The size of the image instance can be modified by this operator. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Assign pixels values from a specified expression. 

Initialize all pixel values from the specified string {\ttfamily expression}. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em expression} & Value string describing the way pixel values are set. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item String parameter {\ttfamily expression} may describe different things\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item If {\ttfamily expression} is a list of values (as in {\ttfamily "{}1,2,3,8,3,2"{}}), or a formula (as in {\ttfamily "{}(x\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}y)\%255"{}}), the pixel values are set from specified {\ttfamily expression} and the image size is not modified.
\item If {\ttfamily expression} is a filename (as in {\ttfamily "{}reference.\+jpg"{}}), the corresponding image file is loaded and replace the image instance. The image size is modified if necessary. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
\begin{DoxyParagraph}{Example}

\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{CImg<float>\ img1(100,100),\ img2(img1),\ img3(img1);\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Declare\ three\ 100x100\ scalar\ images\ with\ unitialized\ pixel\ values.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img1\ =\ \textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}0,50,100,150,200,250,200,150,100,50"{}};\ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Set\ pixel\ values\ of\ 'img1'\ from\ a\ value\ sequence.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img2\ =\ \textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}10*((x*y)\%25)"{}};\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Set\ pixel\ values\ of\ 'img2'\ from\ a\ formula.}}
\DoxyCodeLine{img3\ =\ \textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}reference.jpg"{}};\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Set\ pixel\ values\ of\ 'img3'\ from\ a\ file\ (image\ size\ is\ modified).}}
\DoxyCodeLine{(img1,img2,img3).\mbox{\hyperlink{structcimg__library__suffixed_1_1CImg_a901c891242e27a7e5bf7932767e80d60}{display}}();}

\end{DoxyCode}
  
\end{DoxyParagraph}

Compute correspondence map between two images, using the patch-\/match algorithm. 


\begin{DoxyParams}[1]{Parameters}
 & {\em patch\+\_\+image} & The image containing the reference patches to match with the instance image. \\
\hline
 & {\em patch\+\_\+width} & Width of the patch used for matching. \\
\hline
 & {\em patch\+\_\+height} & Height of the patch used for matching. \\
\hline
 & {\em patch\+\_\+depth} & Depth of the patch used for matching. \\
\hline
 & {\em nb\+\_\+iterations} & Number of patch-\/match iterations. \\
\hline
 & {\em nb\+\_\+randoms} & Number of randomization attempts (per pixel). \\
\hline
 & {\em guide} & \doxylink{classImage}{Image} used as the initial correspondence estimate for the algorithm. \textquotesingle{}guide\textquotesingle{} may have a last channel with boolean values (0=false \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} other=true) that tells for each pixel if its correspondence vector is constrained to its initial value (constraint mask). \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ out}}  & {\em matching\+\_\+score} & Returned as the image of matching scores. \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
The patch-\/match algorithm is described in this paper\+: Connelly Barnes, Eli Shechtman, Adam Finkelstein, Dan B Goldman(2009), Patch\+Match\+: A Randomized Correspondence Algorithm for Structural \doxylink{classImage}{Image} Editing 
\end{DoxyNote}

Save image as a TIFF file. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em filename} & Filename, as a C-\/string. \\
\hline
{\em compression\+\_\+type} & Type of data compression. Can be {\ttfamily \{ 0=None \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} 1=LZW \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} 2=JPEG \}}. \\
\hline

\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item libtiff support is enabled by defining the precompilation directive {\ttfamily cimg\+\_\+use\+\_\+tif}.
\item When libtiff is enabled, 2D and 3D (multipage) several channel per pixel are supported for {\ttfamily char,uchar,short,ushort,float} and {\ttfamily double} pixel types.
\item If {\ttfamily cimg\+\_\+use\+\_\+tif} is not defined at compile time the function uses CImg$<$\+T$>$\&save\+\_\+other(const char\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}). 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Return the number of image channels. 

Return the number of image channels, i.\+e. the image dimension along the C-\/axis. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The spectrum() of an empty image is equal to {\ttfamily 0}.
\item spectrum() is typically equal to {\ttfamily 1} when considering scalar-\/valued images, to {\ttfamily 3} for RGB-\/coded color images, and to {\ttfamily 4} for RGBA-\/coded color images (with alpha-\/channel). The number of channels of an image instance is not limited. The meaning of the pixel values is not linked up to the number of channels (e.\+g. a 4-\/channel image may indifferently stands for a RGBA or CMYK color image).
\item spectrum() returns an {\ttfamily int}, although the image spectrum is internally stored as an {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int}. Using an {\ttfamily int} is safer and prevents arithmetic traps possibly encountered when doing calculations involving {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variables. Access to the initial {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variable is possible (though not recommended) by {\ttfamily (\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}this).\+\_\+spectrum}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Return a C-\/string containing a list of all values of the image instance. 

Return a new {\ttfamily CImg$<$char$>$} image whose buffer data() is a {\ttfamily char\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}} string describing the list of all pixel values of the image instance (written in base 10), separated by specified {\ttfamily separator} character. 
\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em separator} & A {\ttfamily char} character which specifies the separator between values in the returned C-\/string. \\
\hline
{\em max\+\_\+size} & Maximum size of the returned image. \\
\hline
{\em format} & For float-\/values, tell the printf format used to generate the ascii representation of the numbers. (or {\ttfamily 0} for default representation). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The returned image is never empty.
\item For an empty image instance, the returned string is {\ttfamily "{}"{}}.
\item If {\ttfamily max\+\_\+size} is equal to {\ttfamily 0}, there are no limits on the size of the returned string.
\item Otherwise, if the maximum number of string characters is exceeded, the value string is cut off and terminated by character {\ttfamily \textquotesingle{}\textbackslash{}0\textquotesingle{}}. In that case, the returned image size is {\ttfamily max\+\_\+size + 1}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}

Return the variance of the pixel values. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em variance\+\_\+method} & Method used to estimate the variance. Can be\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily 0}\+: Second moment, computed as  $1/N \sum\limits_{k=1}^{N} (x_k - \bar x)^2 =
1/N \left( \sum\limits_{k=1}^N x_k^2 - \left( \sum\limits_{k=1}^N x_k \right)^2 / N \right)$ with $ \bar x = 1/N \sum\limits_{k=1}^N x_k $.
\item {\ttfamily 1}\+: Best unbiased estimator, computed as $\frac{1}{N - 1} \sum\limits_{k=1}^{N} (x_k - \bar x)^2 $.
\item {\ttfamily 2}\+: Least median of squares.
\item {\ttfamily 3}\+: Least trimmed of squares. 
\end{DoxyItemize}\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Return estimated variance of the noise. 


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em variance\+\_\+method} & Method used to compute the variance (see variance(const unsigned int) const). \\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
Because of structures such as edges in images it is recommanded to use a robust variance estimation. The variance of the noise is estimated by computing the variance of the Laplacian  $(\Delta
I)^2 $ scaled by a factor $c$ insuring  $ c E[(\Delta I)^2]=
\sigma^2$ where $\sigma$ is the noise variance. 
\end{DoxyNote}

Return the number of image columns. 

Return the image width, i.\+e. the image dimension along the X-\/axis. \begin{DoxyNote}{Note}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The width() of an empty image is equal to {\ttfamily 0}.
\item width() is typically equal to {\ttfamily 1} when considering images as {\itshape vectors} for matrix calculations.
\item width() returns an {\ttfamily int}, although the image width is internally stored as an {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int}. Using an {\ttfamily int} is safer and prevents arithmetic traps possibly encountered when doing calculations involving {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variables. Access to the initial {\ttfamily unsigned} {\ttfamily int} variable is possible (though not recommended) by {\ttfamily (\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}this).\+\_\+width}. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
\end{DoxyNote}
